items.source_item: Tool and MCP orchestration policy with minimum-sufficient routing and tool-grounded audits
items.intent: Reduce tool clutter and select an efficient verification route while grounding audit conclusions
items.rationale: The minimum-sufficient capability and evidence-grounding intent is useful. The source hard-codes unadmitted tool names, unsupported latency and token claims, a dimensionally weak score, silent fallback, and mandatory MCP execution. Triton instead filters by admission, evidence need, authority, data and environment before using measured task-specific efficiency and an explicit independently admitted fallback.
items.protected_outcome: Efficient evidence collection without bypassing admission, data boundaries, authority or audit reasoning
items.follow_up_trigger: Representative admitted capability observations support a task-specific change to routing order or fallback

items.source_item: Two-tier reviewer-led execution loop added to AI processing and assurance flow
items.intent: Separate production from independent verification, constrain context, and prevent moving acceptance criteria
items.rationale: Producer-verifier separation, bounded evidence and deterministic-first checks are useful. Immutable acceptance criteria, mandatory subagents and tools, universal two-plus-one loops, zero-cost test claims, and nominal escalation thresholds are unsafe or unevidenced. Triton uses a controlled versioned acceptance baseline, task-specific decomposition and stop conditions, sufficient reviewer context, and explicit partial or human escalation when material evidence remains unresolved.
items.protected_outcome: Independent assurance with bounded cost and context without suppressing valid dissent or inventing universal process strength
items.follow_up_trigger: Measured rework, escaped defects or review delay indicates that a project-specific loop budget or evidence packet needs adjustment

items.source_item: Antigravity response and progress note claiming 41 checks, clean state, three modified files and zero escaped defects
items.intent: Communicate the external implementation and its claimed verification evidence
items.rationale: The note is useful as a statement of intent but not as acceptance evidence. The source is a Git repository, but the reviewed increment was not committed and git status contradicted its clean-tree claim: three reviewed paths were modified and the response note was untracked. Four same-day files were observed rather than the declared three, zero escaped defects is unsupported, and its 41-check baseline does not establish Triton fitness. The authoritative Triton baseline independently passed 54 checks before this adaptation.
items.protected_outcome: Traceable external feedback without converting self-reported status into Triton operational truth
items.follow_up_trigger: Antigravity supplies a commit-backed increment and independently reproducible evidence for a later review

items.source_item: Corporate pulse state containing active project, model, milestone, decision and health claims
items.intent: Provide a current company-wide operating view
items.rationale: The state mixes Ralja product content into the Company OS, asserts unverified active models and completed capabilities, records test and role decisions as binding, and presents inconsistent green health counts. Copying it would create false authority, stale operational truth and a workspace-boundary violation. Triton's pulse remains a read-only projection of controlled evidence statements.
items.protected_outcome: Truthful evidence-bound founder reporting and strict separation of corporate configuration from product workspaces
items.follow_up_trigger: A controlled evidence source provides validated pulse statements or a sanitised project export through the admitted boundary
